keyframe_review.note: 277,000 km2 on the Pontic steppe between the Dniester and the Don (26.3-39.1 E, 44.9-50.3 N), 1056-1065. No state of Halych or Volhynia exists in these years: 'The Principality of Galicia was formed in the years 1124-1144' and 'Galicia and Volhynia merged around 1198 or 1199'; the Kingdom page does not place either state on the steppe. Checked with the gazetteer, the row shares at most 2,000 km2 with Kievan Rus' (1100) and nothing with Cliopatria's Principality of Galicia-Volhynia (1230). The cuman-kipchak-confederation dossier already claims the same steppe (about 830 cells, 29-39 E).

correction.text: no Galician-Volhynian land: the cells of this shape are Pecheneg and Cuman steppe (cuman-kipchak-confederation, pechenegs), none is Halych-Volhynia territory

Yaroslav Osmomysl (1152-1187) is the one reign in which the Halych page has Galician power near the steppe: 'the consolidation of Galician influence in the lower reaches of the Dniester, Prut, and Danube rivers' (undated, 'influence' not rule). That is a strip along the rivers, not 400,000 km2 of steppe; the Cumans were the Galician princes' enemies ('campaigns against the Cumans'). A gap-filler for principality-of-halych should decide whether the Dniester-Prut-Danube strip is a client region.

ledger.note: 1056: Cliopatria begins a 'Halych-Volhynia occupation' row on the Pontic steppe. No page opened shows a Galician or Volhynian state in 1056 or on this land; the dossier exists to record that the row is mis-attributed and carries no territory of its own (type umbrella).

region.text: Cliopatria's first shape of the row: the steppe between the Dniester and the Don

ledger.note: 1240: the row ends with the Mongol invasion. 'the horde stormed Kiev in December 1240'; the cities of Halych and Volodymyr 'were devastated by the Mongols' in 1240 (Kingdom page); the Cuman confederacy ceased 'in 1241' (Cumania page). The land of the row passes to the Mongol Empire (Ulus Jochi) as the steppe the Cumans had held; no Galician-Volhynian land is lost by this row.

wars.name: Roman Mstislavich's campaigns against the Cumans
wars.outcome: 'mounted two successful campaigns against the Cumans, in 1201-2 and 1203-4'; the page gives no territorial result.
wars.note: Raids; the page also says the state 'briefly controlled the Brodnici on the Black Sea' without a date and with a citation flag.

wars.name: Daniel of Galicia against the Bolokhoveni
wars.outcome: The Bolokhovian princes 'were in constant conflict with Daniel, the prince of Galicia-Volhynia, between 1231 and 1257' and 'disappeared after Daniel defeated them in 1257'; they besieged Kamianets-Podilskyi in 1233 or 1235 and 1236, and Daniel 'invaded and pillaged the Bolokhovian Land' in 1241.
wars.note: Not a conquest on the page's account; the Bolokhovian Land lay 'between the Dniester and Dnieper rivers' / south of the Khomora, a tributary of the Sluch.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus' (Galicia-Volhynia, 1240-1241)
wars.outcome: The Mongols devastated Halych and Volodymyr in 1240 ('the cities of Halych and Volodymyr were devastated by the Mongols'); Daniel pledged allegiance to Batu in 1246 and paid tribute. Territorial effect belongs to the Galicia-Volhynia dossiers.

certainty.note: The row has no frontier of its own: the steppe edges are approximate and the dossier carries no territory.

notes:
This Cliopatria row is not Halych-Volhynia. Its 10 shapes (277,000-452,000 km2, 1056-1240) lie on the Pontic steppe from the Dniester and the lower Danube to the Don, with a western extension to 22.5 E (Wallachia) in 1066-1205; the gazetteer shows 2,000 km2 of overlap with Kievan Rus' (1100) and none with Cliopatria's Principality of Galicia-Volhynia (188,000 km2, 1202-1240), Halych, Terebovlia, Peremyshl, Volhynia, Kiev, Pereyaslavl, Chernigov, Hungary, the Byzantine Empire or the Second Bulgarian Empire (each checked in a year of its life). It touches every neighbour without overlapping one: it reads as a fill of the land no other Cliopatria row covers, not as a state. No page opened places Halych, Volhynia or the Kingdom of Galicia-Volhynia on this land; the pages put the Cumans there. The row therefore is a mis-attribution, and all ten shapes are 'wrong' with an empty correction (the `minus` of the shape from itself, which the gazetteer reports as a region with no cells on purpose). The dossier is type umbrella (no territory of its own) so the colour agent should not seed a colour for it.

Shared Wikidata Q239502 with principality-of-galicia-volhynia and galicia-volhynia: different things, not one state. The row is not merged; those two rows are real Galicia-Volhynia (1202-1240 and 1294-1351) and belong to the other eu-16 agents.

Decision needed from the compile stage: the same steppe is claimed by cuman-kipchak-confederation (about 830 cells, 29-39 E, 1056-1241) and by the Pecheneg dossier (1043-1090). The part of this row west of 29 E (Wallachia and Moldavia to 22.5 E in 1066-1205, 'White Cumania ... eastern Wallachia, Black Cumania ... Moldavia' on the Cumania page) is not in the Cuman dossier's Pontic Steppe region and would become nobody's land; the Cuman agent should add Wallachia and Moldavia, or the Wallachian row be sent to a Romania/Balkans agent (it is Cuman country on the page; Bulgarian Second Empire and Hungary border it from 1188 and 1066).

Page-supported facts for the other eu-16 agents (principality-of-halych, principality-of-galicia-volhynia): Galician influence in the lower Dniester, Prut and Danube in Osmomysl's reign 1152-1187 (undated); the Cumans fought 1201-02 and 1203-04; the Brodnici on the Black Sea 'briefly controlled' (undated, flagged); Daniel took Kiev in 1239 and 'had taken Kiev under his protection the previous year' (Mongol invasion page); the Bolokhoveni war 1231-1257. These are not ledger events of this dossier.
